# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book should not exist.
There are already so many free available materials online.
Many universities have materials and open courses (examples).
There are PDF and books available.
There are videos on YouTube, some might be more legitimate than others.
I also hope that there are libraries where you are and you have access to recent up-to-date physical books...if you are student do not hesitate to make a request to your advisors and acquaintances, still stay reasonable.
As far as know, foreign researchers are not shy on bringing knowledge. Just ask!!!
And ultimately, I expect that the major part of what is written here are taught during undergraduate and graduate courses at your institutions.

So is there a need for this book?
Well, I aim and try to address superficial problems with this book.
The first problem is decentralized information.
Maybe there is a book on coding and another book on statistics.
Maybe in some books, the basics are not covered so you need to look somewhere else.
Maybe the levels differ.
The first aim to gather in one place multiple informations, maybe this handbook has an encyclopedia philosophy.
This early realize for instance includes basic knowledge, with beginner level. basic math vs intermediate math, descriptive statistics vs statistical inference etc.

Second, focus on intuition and examples. Definition are added for comprehensive where random because who doesn't like sopopa. this handbook/encyclopedia is written in a compact form to combine the intuitive, the formal, and applied perspectives.
Each topic will be divided into 5 parts although there are exceptions .
The first part will provide the intuition for the concept, I will use metaphor etc. This book is written for Malagasy first so many concepts will be based on Malagasy culture etc.
The second part will focus on the formal definition which could be Googled, and generally encounter in other books or teaching materials. This could be boring in the first phase as it is difficult to define concept in first principle.
The third part will provide a practical side, how to run those things in R.
The fourth part will provide tips and warnings which

Third, this is free book, you can download it from principally my webpage and probably other pages.
Feel free to share it with anyone, use on whatever you want but this is self-edited book so you should not use it as a valid citation.
As the proverb says, _Saonjo iray lohasa_.
Someone might try to make a business out of it.
I am sorry for those who will pay for it and get scammed.

As a warning, it is worth mentioning that I am no expert in any of the topics and sections.
I am mostly self-taught training in statistics and programming.
There are experts in the field, and I should be the absolute reference.
This book is based on my own experience and the way how I understand the concept, the way how I code.
This is more a generalist approach to the concept.
<!-- Yet, to enhance the value, I had colleagues and past advisors--the experts--that made sure that what is written is not completely nonsense.
I am grateful and forever in dept to Otso, Tony, Guillaume, Gavin, Eva.
However, if there is something wrong, I take full responsibility. -->

About on AI: AI is another blooming stuff and seems like a obvious approach.
In fact, I used AI to help polishing the book.
However, I have a fear of overeliance/dependence and do not recommend reliance on its usuage without sufficient foundational and criticial thinking about the topic. Hopefully, this book can provide such basic understanding.
